Field.Label: SOLAR FORECAST (Open-Meteo — no API key required)

Arrays are modelled using Open-Meteo free GTI data (10,000 calls/day limit). Site coordinates have NO built-in default — fill them in below for your own roof, or set LATITUDE / LONGITUDE in IndigoSecrets.py. If neither is set the plugin logs an ERROR and skips the solar forecast. Example: Big Ben, London is 51.5007, -0.1246. The arrays field expects a JSON list — leave blank to use the built-in default.

PV array specs (JSON list of {name, tilt, azimuth, kwp, shade}, blank = defaults):

Example (one line per array, paste as a single JSON line): [{"name":"South","tilt":34,"azimuth":-13,"kwp":4.275,"shade":0.86},{"name":"West","tilt":32,"azimuth":77,"kwp":2.850,"shade":0.85}]. tilt=degrees from horizontal (0=flat, 90=vertical), azimuth=Open-Meteo convention (0=South, 90=West, -90=East, 180=North). If the JSON fails to parse, the built-in default is used and an ERROR is logged.
Battery module size (kWh, for working out how many packs you have):
Battery pack count (blank = work it out from capacity / module size):

The inverter reports one average temperature for the whole battery plus the hottest and coldest of its packs — it does not report each pack separately. Those three figures are still enough to tell whether one pack is out of step with the others, which is what the dashboards show. That needs the pack count: a SigenStor module is 8.76 kWh, so 35.04 kWh divides to 4. Set the count directly if your stack is different.
PV string names (comma-separated, in PV1..PV4 order; blank = PV1, PV2...):

Names the inverter's per-string readings on the dashboards. Optionally add each string's kWp after a colon so its bar can be scaled to capacity — e.g. "South:4.275, East:4.275, West:2.85, NE:2.85". The order is the inverter's own PV input order, which may not match the array order above; watch each string's morning/evening curve on a clear day to identify them before naming.
OCTOPUS ENERGY (credentials in IndigoSecrets.py take priority)

Export MPAN/serial are optional. When set, the plugin compares the inverter's daily export against Octopus's settled half-hourly readings (last 7 settled days, ±5% tolerance) on the Export Sync dashboard card. Settlement typically takes 24-48 h, so the most recent three days are skipped.
Gas calorific factor (kWh per m3, optional — default ~11.19). Set this to the exact figure on your Octopus bill for penny-accurate gas costs.

kWh — some SMETS2 meters report kWh directly (no conversion)

Field.Label: Gas MPRN/serial are optional. When set, the Whole-house cost dashboard card adds your settled daily gas cost (unit + standing charge) to the electric cost, valued from the Octopus account ledger. Gas settles roughly a day in arrears, so today's gas figure is an estimate until then. Daily-read gas meters (one reading per day) are supported. If you have no gas meter, the card shows electricity only.

An empty house draws a flat base load with none of the usual daily shape, so planning against the normal profile buys for people who are not there. Point this at an Indigo variable your holiday schedules already set, and the plugin keeps a second consumption profile for the days the house is empty. The two never mix, so a long trip cannot skew the normal one either. If the variable is missing or unreadable the house is treated as occupied.

The plugin serves a live dashboard on port 8179. Until v5.75.0 it listened on every network interface and asked for nothing, so anyone on your network could read your energy, tariff and VPP data. It now listens on this machine only, which is the right setting for almost everyone: the Dashboards plugin fetches this data through a server-side proxy, so its Energy and Cost pages work exactly as before. Choose "Whole network" only if you want to open http://<server>:8179/ from a phone, tablet or another computer. Doing so requires an access token, and the plugin will refuse to start the dashboard without one. Use Plugins -> Sigenergy Manager -> Show Web Dashboard Access to get the link.

Leave blank and the plugin generates a strong token for you and stores it in its own data folder, readable only by this user. Set SIGEN_DASHBOARD_TOKEN in IndigoSecrets.py to override both. Never expose port 8179 to the internet by forwarding a port — use Tailscale or a Cloudflare Tunnel instead.

Only affects the address the plugin advertises for the dashboard. Leave blank to auto-detect the LAN IP, or set DASHBOARD_HOST in IndigoSecrets.py, or type a hostname or static IP your other devices can reach.
PUSHOVER NOTIFICATIONS (credentials in IndigoSecrets.py take priority)

Pushover alerts are sent for storm warnings and VPP release failures. The Pushover Indigo plugin must be installed and enabled. Provide the recipient user/group key here OR in IndigoSecrets.py as PUSHOVER_USER_TOKEN. If neither is set, alerts will be skipped and a warning will be logged.
Quiet hours start (HH:MM, e.g. 22:00 — blank = none):
Quiet hours end (HH:MM, e.g. 07:00 — blank = none):
During quiet hours, INFO-level (non-emergency) Pushover alerts are suppressed. HIGH-priority alerts (storm amber/red, VPP release failure) always fire regardless.

When the inverter reports the grid has been lost (the house islands onto the battery) and again when mains power is restored, send an alert. The Pushover alert uses the settings above and is sent at normal priority, so it respects quiet hours. Email is sent via the Email+ SMTP device. Note: a longer outage may also take your broadband down, in which case the alert is delivered once connectivity returns.
Email recipient address. IndigoSecrets.py (POWERCUT_EMAIL) takes priority over this field. Leave both blank to send Pushover only.

After the grid is restored, export is held off for a few hours as a precaution — but only while the battery is below this percentage. At or above it, export resumes so flood-prevention can shed surplus and a near-full battery doesn't reach 100% and clip solar. Default 85.

Export also resumes during the lockout when the day's remaining solar comfortably refills the battery to the floor above on its own — on a bright summer morning, holding export off banks nothing the sun wasn't going to deliver anyway, and only risks driving the battery to 100% and clipping everything above your export cap. This setting is the safety line: however good the forecast looks, that early release never applies below this percentage, because a nearly-empty battery is not a resilience reserve. On a winter night, with no solar to come, the SOC floor above governs on its own. Default 50.

On a sunny day the battery charge is paced to reach this level by dusk, and everything spare is exported. This is a target, not a limit — once export is running at your DNO cap, surplus solar has nowhere else to go and keeps charging the battery past it, so most bright days still finish near full. Aiming at 100% is counter-productive: the pacing is taken out of export before the cap is applied, so a high target spends the morning giving away exportable units to buy charge, and still meets the afternoon peak with less room to absorb it. Default 90.

Safety net for the configured pacing target. The daytime overflow gate already stops export as soon as the remaining forecast can no longer fill the battery to 100%, so every spare unit is then kept. This floor prevents a mis-set target below the resilience level you want available for a power cut. Default 80.

No inverter setting is changed. The daily record compares the early export made available by the live 90% pacing with a 95% pacing estimate, then records observed end SOC, export and evening imports. It also prices the same observed imports at Tracker and published Agile half-hourly rates. This is evidence for a later decision, not an Agile dispatch simulation.

During an active storm warning, export is held off so the battery banks charge ahead of a possible power cut — but only while it is below this percentage. At or above it the reserve is already banked, so export resumes (Solar Overflow throttles the charge and pushes surplus to grid) rather than ramming the battery to 100% and clipping every watt of PV above your export cap. Never drops below the storm reserve target (50% yellow / 80% amber-red). Default 85.
